faq: Where can I find the templates?
Explore a template’s previews and skins here, then open it on ChatStyle for current pricing and customization.
How do I add an overlay to OBS?
After setting it up in ChatStyle, add the overlay URL as a browser source in your OBS scene. Adjust its size and position in your scene.
Think about color, readability and movement alongside your game or camera. Our [quick overlay guide](/ratgeber/chat-overlay-auswaehlen/) helps you choose.

guide.title: Choose the right chat overlay | Stream design guide
guide.description: Find a chat overlay that fits your stream: check style, readability, chat width and motion with real design examples.
heading: A great look
reads well.
guide.intro: Your chat should feel like you, and your community should be able to read it. These four checks help you find a design that works in your actual stream.
sections: Look at your camera, panels and the games you stream. Pick an element to echo in your chat: an accent color, a shape or a mood. Try [Lofi Windows 93](/overlays/lofi-windows-93/) for a nostalgic desktop feel, or [Chat Garden](/overlays/chat-garden/) for a botanical scene.
2. Give your chat the right space.

An overlay needs to handle short and long messages. Decide between a dedicated chat column and a free corner of your scene. Slim designs such as [Inline Flow](/overlays/inline-flow/) and [Small Talk](/overlays/small-talk/) suit compact layouts. Decorative designs need more space around their bubbles.

Try your overlay over both light and dark gameplay. Then shrink the entire scene: can you still read names and messages? Pixel styles such as [Retromon Silver](/overlays/retromon-silver/) need enough text size. Floral details should never cover the words.

A still image shows the style; the original video shows the pace. See how the chat works alongside your camera and alerts. If your scene already has lots of movement, a calmer chat may work better. Compare [Violet Frame](/overlays/violet-frame/) with the more compact [Violet Frame Slim](/overlays/violet-frame-slim/).
guide.callout: Open the template on ChatStyle to see current pricing and available settings. You can then set up your overlay there.

neon-cyber.name: Neon & Cyber
neon-cyber.intro: Glowing outlines, terminal windows and digital details. Chat overlays for dark gaming scenes, sci-fi and technical setups.
neon-cyber.tip: Keep neon lines visible against your background. A calm area behind the chat and a few repeating accent colors help the scene feel consistent.

cozy-cute.name: Cozy & Cute
cozy-cute.intro: Pastel colors, flowers and little characters for relaxed streams. Find a chat overlay that feels like part of your community.
cozy-cute.tip: Check the contrast between light bubbles and your scene. Leave space around decorations, your camera and alerts so messages remain the focus.

retro-pixel.name: Retro & Pixel
retro-pixel.intro: From classic desktop windows to arcade dialogues: chat overlays for retro games, pixel worlds and digital nostalgia.
retro-pixel.tip: Pixel fonts need enough size. Check a smaller preview of your entire scene, since many viewers watch on their phones.

clean-minimal.name: Clean & Minimal
clean-minimal.intro: Slim bubbles, clean lines and plenty of room for your content. Subtle designs that complement your scene.
clean-minimal.tip: Test your chat column with long names, emotes and multiline messages. Minimal designs feel calm when their spacing works in real use.

dark-gothic.name: Dark & Gothic
dark-gothic.intro: Dark surfaces, ornate frames and distinctive themes. Explore chat designs for fantasy, horror and atmospheric streams.
dark-gothic.tip: Dark designs need clear text contrast. Check the overlay in light and dark game scenes and watch its animated effects before using it.
